ideas.title: Icom's New Amateur Transceiver FCC Filing and the IC-7110: What We Know
ideas.why_now: Icom filed an FCC application for an amateur transceiver on November 6. The IC-7110 (the former X-026) was just revealed overseas, and US hams want to know when it arrives. A filing is not a product yet, so this is a careful look at what the paperwork shows.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN 2026-11-12 YouTube slot. This is a new angle on the earlier Icom filing pitches. Those covered VHF and UHF digital transceivers, which may be commercial gear. This filing is labeled amateur. Walk through the filing, compare it to what we saw of the X-026 at Hamvention, and be clear about what is confirmed and what is guesswork. Cut a Short from the filing reveal.

ideas.title: The FCC Test Lab Ruling: What It Means for Your Next Xiegu, Quansheng or Wouxun
ideas.why_now: The FCC voted to end certification through non-reciprocal foreign test labs, and radio listings without a valid FCC ID are now banned at the point of sale. Budget radio buyers want to know whether the imports they like will keep coming, especially heading into holiday shopping.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN 2026-11-19 YouTube slot, before Black Friday. The earlier eBay pitch and Ep. 23 were about selling used gear on eBay. This one is about certification: how radios get approved, what happens to brands that rely on overseas labs, and what to check before you buy. Use our own Xiegu G7250 as the example. Also note the recent Wouxun and Retevis filings as proof that new FCC IDs are still being granted.

ideas.title: RADE vs SSB On the Air: FreeDV Digital Voice in Half the Bandwidth
ideas.why_now: RADE is the biggest HF voice story right now. It fits voice into about 1.5 kHz, works down to -2 dB SNR, has FlexRadio integration shipping, and v2 in testing aims for under 1 kHz.
ideas.angle: Record at the OPEN 2026-12-01 session for release in the OPEN 2026-12-03 podcast slot. The earlier pitch bundled RADE with JTTY on budget radios and phones. This is the hosts' dedicated hands-on episode instead: what RADE is, a live on-air A/B of RADE and SSB audio, and plain talk about whether everyday hams should try it this winter. The title is a statement, not the host's question, because question titles underperform. Clip the A/B audio into a Short.

ideas.title: CQ WW CW Weekend From the Shack: Fresh DX on the FTdx101MP #cqww #contest
ideas.why_now: CQ World Wide CW runs November 28 and 29. The 2026 rules require a human to start frequency changes, station calls and QSO logging, and that rule applies to assisted entries too.
ideas.angle: A Short shot live during contest weekend, shown in the days after Thanksgiving. It doesn't use a YouTube slot. Repeat last year's winning format: the band full of DX, a few quick contacts, and one line on the new human-in-the-loop rule. Contest content is weak as edited video for this channel, so keep it short-form only.

ideas.title: POTACAT on an Icom IC-7300: Hunting Parks From Home With a Free App
ideas.why_now: A free app for remote park hunting is breaking out on another channel right now. Winter is when Michigan hams hunt parks from the shack instead of activating.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN 2026-12-10 YouTube slot. It's framed as software plus a branded HF rig, not a POTA trip, because park content underperforms here. Set it up on our shack IC-7300, hunt a handful of parks, and show what it does compared with PoLo and the POTA site. This is a new tool, separate from the QRV app, HTCommander and POTA website pitches.

ideas.title: Free Browser Decoders for SSTV, APRS and Weather Fax With an RTL-SDR
ideas.why_now: SDR talk is the fastest rising discussion topic. New free decoders now run entirely in a web browser, so you can try SSTV, APRS, RTTY and weather fax with nothing to install.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN 2026-12-17 YouTube slot, a good low-cost holiday project. This is a new angle on the iPad and Android FT8 pitch: browser-only tools and several modes. Plug in a dongle, open a page, and decode real signals. Include an ISS pass if one lines up, and cut that into a Short.

ideas.title: New Baofeng or Quansheng Under the Tree: Your First Week on the Local Repeater
ideas.why_now: Lots of new handhelds get unwrapped at Christmas, and new ham discussion is already climbing. This is a practical first-week guide for when the box gets opened.
ideas.angle: Fits the OPEN 2026-12-24 YouTube slot, or 2026-12-31 if the gift guide takes the earlier dates. Cover programming a Michigan repeater, checking into a first net, and the beginner mistakes to skip. This is a how-to, unlike the earlier 'Keeping New Hams on the Air' discussion pitch and the DMR handheld comparison.
